 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Minnesota Timberwolves look like a budding juggernaut in the 2026-27 NBA season.
 They beat the Heat on the road by 25 in the season opener. They went up to Orlando on Friday and beat the Magic by 22. And on Sunday, in their first game of the season at Target Center, the Wolves crushed the 2-0 Raptors by 23, winning 117-94 to move to 3-0.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Toronto was without star Kawhi Leonard, but still, this was a complete bludgeoning in Minneapolis. The Wolves were up eight points at half and then won the third quarter by 20. They shot 56 percent from the floor and 48 percent from three. The Raptors shot 38 and 26 percent. Toronto's other star, Scottie Barnes, went 0 for 12 in 27 minutes and did not score a point for just the second time in his six-year NBA career.
 With the win, the Timberwolves joined the 1962-63 Boston Celtics and the 2004-05 Utah Jazz as the third team in NBA history to win their first three games of the season by at least 20 points.
 After a dud in Orlando, Anthony Edwards led the Timberwolves with 26 points on 10-of-18 shooting. LaMelo Ball played only 17 minutes due to some foul trouble, but the Wolves won those minutes by 33 points. Ball scored 15 points with four threes and eight assists. Jonathan Kuminga and Terrence Shannon Jr. combined to make six of their seven threes.
 Through three games, Timberwolves fans should be elated by what they've seen from their team. It's been beautiful basketball, with contributions coming from all over. Although it's obviously extremely early, the Wolves' combination of star power and depth makes them look like a legitimate contender moving forward.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement One possible concern
 If there's one area of concern for the Timberwolves, it's that their superstar doesn't exactly appear to be 100 percent healthy. Yes, Edwards scored 45 points in the opener and put up an efficient 26 in this game. He also, on multiple occasions, was seen favoring the right knee that has given him trouble in the past.
 After a wide-open dunk in the second quarter, Edwards grabbed at that knee and seemed to be in a bit of discomfort as he jogged back the other way. In the third quarter, Edwards was fouled by Immanuel Quickley in transition and was again clearly favoring his right knee as he took a moment on the ground before letting teammates help him up.
 Edwards missed time with inflammation in his right knee last season. He's also dealt with a condition called "runner's knee" on that side. Separately, he missed time in last year's playoffs after hyperextending his left knee in the first round. Edwards said he took about two months off this offseason to give his knees time to heal. That the right one is still giving him trouble at the start of a new season is at least slightly concerning.
